quantities.V1: prosthodontic case fee for the appliance (bridge, denture or space maintainer), in dollars
quantities.V2: patient caries/periodontal risk ratio from the preventive-care chart (expected remake or failure fraction)
quantities.V3: lab adjustment and chair-time cost for fitting and re-fitting the appliance, in dollars
quantities.V4: schedule parameter (insurer allowable fee basis for the procedure code)
quantities.ANNEX_SEVERITY: severity of the clinical annex exception (infection-control incident or contraindicating oral-health finding)

tier3_rule: billed_fee * (1 - REG.remake_writeoff_rate * eff_sev) - REG.lab_chargeback * REG.periodontal_failure_mult * V3
draft.rationale: A general dentist's case file for a prosthodontic appliance centres on the case fee (V1), blended with the insurer allowable (V4) to give a billed fee, plus lab and chair-time fitting costs (V3). The patient's caries/periodontal risk ratio (V2) comes from the preventive-care advice task and drives remake risk. The annex severity captures an infection-control incident or contraindicating finding. The handbook prints the following rules: a standard fitting fee, a remake-warranty reduction proportional to risk, and an explicit hold that discounts the fee when an infection-control or clinical exception is documented. The unwritten convention is that practitioners discount more steeply for high-risk patients (risk ratio of 14% or above) when an exception is present, absorbing extra fitting cost and crediting part of the allowable. The precedent covers periodontal failure: severity is amplified by risk through a private failure multiplier, with a registry write-off rate and a lab chargeback applied to fitting costs.
